newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 13.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
- The Dow Jones Industrial average dropped 1.5 percent in an all-day decline that was capped with a 46-point dive in the last half-hour of trading.
- Mexico raised import tariffs on eight American products in response to a recent decision in Washington to punish Mexican straw broom makers with higher duties.
- The Miller Brewing Co, owned by Philip Morris, is withdrawing creative responsibilities for its biggest brands from two big advertising agencies.
- BankAmerica said it would eliminate 3,700 of its 92,700 jobs and close 120 of its 1,017 branches in California.
- Shoppers kept a wary eye on spending as this year's late holiday shopping season got underway.
- The Federal pension insurance agency said the shortfall last year between promised pension benefits and the money set aside to pay for them grew to $64 billion.
- Siemens of Germany, which has already made big work force cuts, said it would dismiss 6,000 employees.
- Western Resources said it would sell its natural gas pipeline and plants to Oneok for $660 million in stock.
- As the end of the World Trade Organization's first meeting neared, representatives compromised over whether the group should push for better standards for workers.
- Charles Schwab said it would make a program that sells 600 mutual funds, at no fee, available to other financial institutions.
- A takeover battle for a New Hampshire company that makes devices that fold and seal cardboard boxes has taken on broad interest because of the state's response to the hostile bid.
- A group of judges and law professors is seeking to have major documents from all securities class-action lawsuits posted in at least one place on the Internet.
